modes.condensate: driven aft to the manifold (evaporator) by the acceleration: assists the wick

cryo.redundancy: two cooler heads per station, each 62.5 % of the station need (installed 125 %): one head lost keeps 62.5 %, so the vessel warms slowly and its neighbours cannot help; recovery = head swap (ORU, LOG-G1 class) within the vessel's thermal hold time
flows: heat lifted from the 3 K and 20 K stages
heat rejected to LOW at 316 K (input + lift)
cryo.explain: CP4 quoted 934 kW = the INSTALLED input (operating x 1.25) and 776 kW for LOW, which mixed the scaled production rejection with installed nuclear terms: two bases, not a lost energy flow. Now every watt has one destination: 822 kW of operating input from the L2 bus plus 6433 W lifted from the cold stages leave as 828 kW into LOW at 316 K (the input is 5 % above the 300 K value because the coolers reject warmer). At full installed capacity (re-cool after a fault) LOW sees 1035 kW for hours, inside its 20 % margin.
cryo.radiation_note: nuclear heating comes from the Phase VI OpenMC surrogate (simplified source and structure): a sensitivity, not a validated shielding result

conductor.rule: L1 conductors sized for the reactive peak (minutes at burnout), not the proactive continuous load; two half-rated segments on separate routes (az 30 and az 150)

converter.note: the 100 MWe FT-04 rating (CONDITIONAL) is the converter rating; it covers the reactive peak with 9.2 MW to spare; the defense burst comes from the buffer, not the pickup

thermal.sink: HOT loop (H6a), inside the HOT budget below
thermal.peak_duration: the reactive peak lasts while a defense engagement runs at burnout; the buffer covers 10 s bursts; minutes-long peaks are HOT-limited (budget below), not conductor-limited

electrical.note: The H6a pumps (10 MW) run from L1 in a burn. With the pickup lost they must come from L2 (8.7 MW EOL, demand ~5.5 MW): they cannot all run, so a pickup fault means a controlled drive shutdown (decay heat goes to the H6a at part flow, 0.15 of the pump power, which L2 can carry). This is an existing Phase V/VI rule and is stated here, not solved.

l2_failure.case: one NaK loop of unit 1 lost (unit feeds only its own blade): fixed split loads that blade to 125 %
l2_failure.derating: faulted unit to 66 % on its remaining loop, the other two at 100 % with biased splits: 7.00 MWe of 10.5

sequence: 0 s: loop low-flow trip on the faulted unit
< 2 s: flow-control valves rebias the neighbouring units (67/33 class)
< 5 s: TAC bypass sets the faulted unit back (turbine bypass to the recuperator); the overloaded blade gains < 50 K in 92 s
1-3 min: reactor ramp-down of the faulted unit to hot standby (decay heat on its own loop A)
L2 load shedding of discretionary loads if the demand band is above the derated output

recovery: isolate the failed loop (isolation valves at the root and the gas cooler)
diagnose: EM pump ORU swap (robot, coast) or a leak (drain to the NaK reserve, sectional repair = yard if the leak is in the casing-hull annulus)
refill, warm the loop with the unit's decay heat, rebias, return to strategy C
l2_failure.verdict: safe degraded state without full output: 2 units + standby carry the coast and burn demand bands except the highest, which sheds discretionary loads

eclss.failing: ring A lost + B unit + hub unit failed
